SIYARAM SILK MILLS Q2 CONCALL: MANAGEMENT RAISES FY27 REVENUE GROWTH GUIDANCE TO 14–15%, TARGETS ₹160 CR RETAIL REVENUE, 70 STORES BY FY27-END & ₹100 CR CAPEX

• MANAGEMENT RAISES FY27 REVENUE GROWTH GUIDANCE TO 14–15%, SUPPORTED BY STRONG FABRIC DEMAND, FESTIVE & WEDDING-SEASON SALES AND EXPANDING RETAIL OPERATIONS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS STRONGER FESTIVE & WEDDING-SEASON DEMAND IN Q3 FY27, PARTICULARLY ACROSS TIER 2 & TIER 3 MARKETS, SUPPORTING FABRIC & APPAREL SALES

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS APPROXIMATELY ₹160 CR RETAIL REVENUE IN FY27, WITH ZCODE & DEVO EXPECTED TO CONTRIBUTE AROUND 5–7% OF TOTAL COMPANY TURNOVER

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS 70 OPERATIONAL RETAIL STORES BY FY27-END, UP FROM 61 CURRENTLY, WITH FUTURE EXPANSION PRIMARILY LED BY ZCODE

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS DEVO STORE COUNT TO STABILIZE AROUND 20–25, WHILE ZCODE EXPANSION CONTINUES ACROSS SOUTHERN INDIA

• MANAGEMENT MAINTAINS APPROXIMATELY 14% UNDERLYING EBITDA MARGIN REFERENCE, WITH RETAIL EXPANSION EXPECTED TO CREATE A MAXIMUM MARGIN DRAG OF AROUND 150 BPS

• MANAGEMENT PLANS FY27 CAPITAL EXPENDITURE OF APPROXIMATELY ₹100 CR, INCLUDING ₹40–50 CR TOWARD RETAIL EXPANSION, FUNDED THROUGH INTERNAL ACCRUALS

• MANAGEMENT HAS IMPLEMENTED CUMULATIVE SELLING-PRICE INCREASES OF APPROXIMATELY 4–6% OVER THE PAST SIX MONTHS TO PARTIALLY OFFSET RISING RAW MATERIAL COSTS

• Q2 TOTAL INCOME GREW 15.1% YOY TO ₹827 CR, WHILE H1 FY27 TOTAL INCOME INCREASED 15.6% TO ₹1,293 CR

• Q2 EBITDA ROSE 8.3% YOY TO ₹131 CR, WITH EBITDA MARGIN AT APPROXIMATELY 15.8%, REFLECTING CONTINUED INPUT-COST PRESSURES

• Q2 PAT DECLINED 13.8% YOY TO ₹75 CR FROM ₹87 CR, PARTLY DUE TO A ₹24 CR NON-RECURRING OTHER-INCOME ITEM IN THE PRIOR-YEAR QUARTER

• H1 FY27 EBITDA STOOD AT ₹170 CR, WHILE PAT REACHED ₹86 CR, WITH DEBT-TO-EQUITY AT 0.58X

• FABRICS CONTRIBUTED APPROXIMATELY 77% OF Q2 REVENUE, FOLLOWED BY GARMENTS AT 16% & YARN AND OTHER SEGMENTS AT 7%

• FABRIC BUSINESS RECORDED APPROXIMATELY 2.5% VOLUME GROWTH & 11% VALUE GROWTH, SUPPORTED BY BETTER PRODUCT MIX & IMPROVING DEMAND

• RETAIL NETWORK EXPANDED TO 61 OPERATIONAL STORES, COMPRISING 38 ZCODE STORES & 23 DEVO STORES

• H1 FY27 RETAIL REVENUE REACHED APPROXIMATELY ₹65 CR, WITH MANAGEMENT TARGETING A SIGNIFICANTLY STRONGER H2 TO ACHIEVE ITS ₹160 CR FULL-YEAR OBJECTIVE

• MANAGEMENT INDICATED SOME RETAIL STORES HAVE ALREADY ACHIEVED STORE-LEVEL EBITDA PROFITABILITY, WHILE NEW STORE INVESTMENTS CONTINUE TO WEIGH ON OVERALL MARGINS

• RETAIL EXPANSION REQUIRES APPROXIMATELY ₹1–1.5 CR PER STORE IN CAPEX & DEPOSITS, ALONG WITH ₹70–80 LAKH IN INVENTORY INVESTMENT

• H1 FY27 CAPEX STOOD AT APPROXIMATELY ₹51 CR, WITH MANAGEMENT EXPECTING FULL-YEAR SPENDING TO REMAIN WITHIN ITS ₹100 CR PLAN

• MANAGEMENT PLANS TO ANNOUNCE FY28 RETAIL STORE EXPANSION & FUNDING GUIDANCE TOWARD THE END OF FY27, AFTER ASSESSING EXISTING STORE PERFORMANCE

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS PREFERENCE-SHARE LISTING APPROVAL TO TAKE AT LEAST ANOTHER SIX MONTHS, WITH APPLICATIONS ALREADY SUBMITTED TO BSE & NSE

• COMPANY DECLARED AN INTERIM DIVIDEND OF ₹4 PER SHARE, WHILE CONTINUING TO FUND RETAIL EXPANSION THROUGH INTERNAL CASH GENERATION

• MANAGEMENT REMAINS POSITIVE ON FY27 REVENUE GROWTH, FESTIVE DEMAND, FABRIC SALES & RETAIL EXPANSION, BUT RAW MATERIAL INFLATION, RETAIL PROFITABILITY, COMPETITION & MARGIN PRESSURE REMAIN KEY RISKS

• MANAGEMENT PLANS TO DIVERSIFY BEYOND AUTOMOTIVE INTO TOOL & DIE STEELS, OIL & GAS, RAILWAYS, BEARINGS, WIND ENERGY, AEROSPACE & DEFENCE, SUPPORTING LONG-TERM HIGHER-VALUE SPECIALTY STEEL DEMAND

• INGOT CASTING EXPECTED TO BEGIN AROUND NOVEMBER 2026, SUPPORTING NEW PRODUCT TRIALS, ALTHOUGH MEANINGFUL NON-AUTOMOTIVE VOLUME CONTRIBUTION IS LIKELY AFTER GREENFIELD CAPACITY COMMISSIONING

• H1 FY27 REVENUE GREW 75.9% YOY TO ₹100.8 CR, EBITDA INCREASED 141.1% TO ₹28.9 CR & NET PROFIT JUMPED 141.3% TO ₹21.24 CR

• H1 EBITDA MARGIN IMPROVED TO 28.7% FROM 20.9% YOY, SUPPORTED BY HIGHER SALES & OPERATING EFFICIENCIES

• CONFIRMED INSTALLED CAPACITY STOOD AT APPROXIMATELY 5.76 LAKH TONNES ANNUALLY, WITH GROUP CAPACITY UTILISATION AROUND 68–69%

• RANCHI PLANT UTILISATION STOOD AT 90–95%, WHILE THE MAIN MONOLITHISCH FACILITY OPERATED AT 55–60%, INDICATING AVAILABLE CAPACITY FOR ADDITIONAL PRODUCTION

• NEW GREENFIELD MANUFACTURING FACILITY COMMENCED OPERATIONS ON 10 OCTOBER 2026, SUPPORTING THE COMPANY'S CAPACITY EXPANSION STRATEGY

• CUSTOMER RETENTION IMPROVED TO A RECORD 73.6% IN Q2 FY27, WHILE QUARTERLY SALES VOLUMES STOOD AT APPROXIMATELY 55,000 TONNES

MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE & EXPECTATIONS

• MANAGEMENT REITERATES FY28 REVENUE TARGET OF OVER ₹500 CR, SUPPORTED BY CAPACITY EXPANSION, MINING INTEGRATION & HIGHER MARKET PENETRATION

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS INCREASING ITS INDIAN RAMMING MASS MARKET SHARE FROM APPROXIMATELY 10% TO 35% OVER THE COMING YEARS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS COMMERCIAL MINING TO BEGIN AROUND 15 JANUARY 2027, WITH A POSSIBLE DELAY OF APPROXIMATELY 15 DAYS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS MINING INTEGRATION TO REDUCE RAW MATERIAL COSTS FROM ₹2,700–3,200 PER TONNE TO ₹1,400–1,500 PER TONNE, WITH ₹300–400 PER TONNE OF SAVINGS POTENTIALLY PASSED TO CUSTOMERS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS NEW GREENFIELD CAPACITY TO REACH PEAK UTILISATION WITHIN 12–18 MONTHS, WITH FURTHER CAPACITY ADDITIONS PLANNED FOR JULY & NOVEMBER 2027

• MANAGEMENT ENVISAGES EXPANDED ANNUAL CAPACITY OF APPROXIMATELY 8.75 LAKH TONNES & AIMS TO DIVERSIFY INTO HIGHER-VALUE SILICA PRODUCTS OVER THE NEXT 2–3 YEARS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS HIGHER VOLUMES & BACKWARD INTEGRATION TO SUPPORT MARGINS, BUT HAS NOT CONFIRMED A 40% EBITDA MARGIN TARGET; MINING EXECUTION, CUSTOMER PRICING & WORKING CAPITAL REMAIN KEY RISKS

INVESTOR TAKEAWAY: POSITIVE OPERATING MOMENTUM, WITH STRONG REVENUE GROWTH, EXPANDING MARGINS & IMPROVING CUSTOMER RETENTION. THE KEY UPCOMING TRIGGER IS COMMERCIAL MINING FROM Q4 FY27, WHICH COULD SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCE RAW MATERIAL COSTS. HOWEVER, THE ₹500+ CR FY28 REVENUE TARGET, EXPECTED COST SAVINGS & CAPACITY RAMP-UP REMAIN MANAGEMENT PROJECTIONS, NOT ACHIEVED RESULTS.

MARKET DEVELOPMENTS – TWO CONTRASTING TRENDS

1. RBI – OVERSEAS CAPITAL FLOWS UNDER SCRUTINY
- Reports suggest tighter scrutiny of large overseas investments and capital outflows.

- However, enhanced scrutiny does not necessarily mean the automatic route has been abolished or all overseas investing is prohibited.

2. NIFTY ON-CHAIN CONTRACTS – 24×7 LEVERAGED TRADING
- Trade[XYZ] launched a synthetic Nifty 50 perpetual contract on Hyperliquid on October 27, 2026.
- Offers 24×7 trading with leverage of up to 20x.
- The contract provides synthetic index exposure, not ownership of Nifty 50 stocks.
- Its launch raises questions around regulatory jurisdiction, offshore derivatives access and legality for Indian residents.
- The launch should not be interpreted as SEBI approval.

3. TAXATION – MARKET SPECULATION
- Discussions around potential tax changes are circulating.
- Any proposed tax relief should be treated as speculation until officially announced.

4. COMMODITIES – POTENTIAL BENEFICIARY
- Commodity trading may attract greater speculative interest amid uncertainty in other markets.
- Higher trading volumes do not automatically translate into higher profitability for every participant.

KEY TAKEAWAY
- Overseas investment scrutiny and the emergence of 24×7 on-chain derivatives represent contrasting developments.
- Commodity markets could benefit from shifting trading activity, but this remains a thesis rather than a confirmed outcome.
- Await official clarification from regulators and exchanges before drawing firm conclusions.

*Nomura: Jio Platforms | India’s telecom pricing reset*

*From volume to value: The Jio story*

India’s telecom sector has grown from a state monopoly into the world’s second-largest subscriber base in around 30 years. Jio’s 2016 launch squeezed a decade of data adoption in two years, and Indians now use ~27GB a month each, according to TRAI data.

Jio’s focus has shifted from adding users to earning more from each customer. Three tariff hikes since 2019 have nearly doubled the company’s mobile broadband ARPU to INR200 in FY26, yet data costs only INR7.5 per GB (vs INR33 in China and INR228 in the US). Indians spend only ~1% of disposable income on connectivity, vs 1.6-2.3% globally, leaving ample room for tariff hikes. With home broadband at only ~21% of households, plus enterprise services and content bundles, we expect the mobile market to grow from INR2.9trn in FY26 to INR5.2tn by FY31F.

Jio, once the disruptor, is now the leader. It has ~42% of the country’s wireless subscribers, ~60% of data traffic and 43% of home broadband. In our view, the listing will likely push Jio Platforms (JPL IN), the price setter, towards steady tariff hikes that peers can follow. We estimate a ~13.5% EBITDA CAGR over FY26-29F. We initiate coverage with a Buy rating and a TP of INR1,340 (based on 12x Dec-2028F EBITDA), implying ~20% upside to the IPO price (INR1,119).

JSW CEMENT – Q2 FY27 RESULTS
#Q2FY27

Financial Highlights
- Total volume sold: 3.93 Mn tonnes, up 26% YoY.
- Cement volume: 2.29 Mn tonnes, up 39% YoY.
- GGBS volume: 1.47 Mn tonnes, up 7% YoY.
- Revenue: ₹1,912 Cr, up 33% YoY.
- Operating EBITDA: ₹277.8 Cr, up 4% YoY.
- Operating EBITDA/tonne: ₹708.
- PAT: ₹77.6 Cr.
- Net debt: ₹4,287 Cr as of September 30, 2026.

Operational Updates
- Strong volume growth driven by cement and GGBS demand across regions, supported by ramp-up in North India.
- Nagar Integrated Unit operated at 75% capacity utilisation and delivered positive operating EBITDA.
- Added 36 MW of wind capacity during the quarter.
- Total renewable capacity, including WHRS, reached 167 MW.

Capacity Expansion – Nagaur
- Commissioned a 1.0 MTPA grinding mill, taking grinding capacity to 3.5 MTPA; clinker capacity stands at 3.3 MTPA.
- Work started on an additional 2.5 MTPA grinding capacity, targeting 6.0 MTPA total capacity.
- Commissioned WHRS, OLBC and AFR co-processing systems to improve cost efficiency.

Shiva Cement Amalgamation
- Boards approved the amalgamation of listed subsidiary Shiva Cement into JSW Cement.
- Aims to create a unified cement platform and unlock operational, financial and management synergies.
- Share-swap ratio: 5 JSW Cement shares for every 41 Shiva Cement shares held by eligible shareholders.
- Transaction is subject to regulatory, shareholder, creditor and NCLT approvals.
- Completion expected in 12–14 months, subject to timely approvals.

H1 FY27 Performance
- Total volume sold: 7.73 Mn tonnes, up 20% YoY.
- Cement volume: 4.63 Mn tonnes, up 33% YoY.
- GGBS volume: 2.80 Mn tonnes, up 5% YoY.
- Revenue: ₹3,809 Cr, up 27% YoY.
- Operating EBITDA: ₹576 Cr, down 2% YoY.
- Operating EBITDA/tonne: ₹745.

Key Takeaway
- Strong revenue and volume growth, capacity expansion and renewable-energy investments support long-term growth.
- However, EBITDA growth lagged revenue growth in Q2, while H1 EBITDA declined 2% YoY, indicating margin pressure.
- Net debt of ₹4,287 Cr and the planned amalgamation remain important monitorables.
- Impact: Mixed to Positive

- Net Interest Income: ₹246.1 Cr, up 31.9% YoY and 6.3% QoQ.

- PAT: ₹170.2 Cr, up 29.1% YoY and 6.5% QoQ.

- ROA: 4.2% vs 3.8% YoY and 4.2% QoQ.

- Credit cost remained contained at 40 bps.

Asset Quality
- GNPA: 1.7% vs 1.9% YoY and 1.8% QoQ.
- NNPA: 1.3% vs 1.5% YoY and 1.4% QoQ.

- 30+ DPD stood at 3.2%.
- Gross Stage 3 declined 10 bps QoQ to 1.7%.
- Focus remains on prudent underwriting, early stress identification and collection discipline.

Business Updates
- Growth driven by healthy demand, deeper penetration in existing markets and distribution investments.
- Added 6 branches, taking the network to 181 branches and 379 touchpoints.
- Added 26 employees net, mainly in customer-facing roles, taking the workforce to 2,014.
- Spreads excluding co-lending moderated by 10 bps, managed through asset pricing, funding costs and liability mix.
- Affordable housing opportunity supported by unmet housing demand, urbanisation and formalisation of incomes.

Management Outlook
- Priorities for the rest of FY27 include sustaining growth, preserving asset quality, protecting profitability and improving operating efficiency.
- Focus on converting growth into consistent earnings, healthy returns and long-term shareholder value.

Key Takeaway
- Strong AUM growth, record disbursements and PAT growth of 29.1% reflect healthy business momentum.
- Improving asset quality and operating efficiency are positives, while spread compression remains a monitorable.
- Impact: Positive

**TATA CONSUMER PRODUCTS – HSBC MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- HSBC maintains **Buy** rating with a target price of ₹1,170.
- Q2FY27 results marginally beat estimates, driven by non-India businesses.
- India business margins remained flat QoQ.
- Growth businesses recorded 40% YoY growth versus 47% in Q1FY27.
- Management continues to focus on 50–70 bps margin improvement.
- HSBC expects 40 bps margin improvement in FY27.
- India margin trajectory remains a key near-term trigger.

**Key Takeaway**
- International business supported the Q2 earnings beat.
- India margin improvement and growth business profitability remain key monitorables.
- Impact: **Positive**

**TATA CONSUMER PRODUCTS – GOLDMAN SACHS MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Goldman Sachs maintains **Buy** rating with a target price of ₹1,325.
- Q2FY27 performance was strong despite a challenging environment, broadly in line with estimates.
- India business delivered 17% revenue growth with double-digit volume growth.
- Management expects pricing growth to accelerate significantly in H2FY27.
- Growth businesses recorded 40% growth, driven by Sampann and ready-to-drink (RTD) products.
- Capital Foods and Organic India domestic growth stood at 24%; exports were impacted by shipping delays.
- Salt business continued strong growth, while tea performance remained muted.
- Management reiterated FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin expansion guidance of 50–70 bps.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong India volume growth and growth businesses support the outlook.
- Pricing improvements and margin expansion remain key H2FY27 catalysts.
- Impact: **Positive**

**TATA CONSUMER PRODUCTS – MORGAN STANLEY MAINTAINS OVERWEIGHT**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Morgan Stanley maintains **Overweight (OW)** rating with a target price of ₹1,202.
- Q2 revenue, EBITDA and adjusted PAT grew 14%, 17% and 18% YoY, respectively.
- Revenue and EBITDA were 1% above estimates, while adjusted PAT was 3% below estimates.
- EBITDA margin stood at 13.8%, up 31 bps YoY and 30 bps QoQ.
- India branded revenue growth accelerated to 17%, versus 13% in each of the previous three quarters.
- India volume growth stood at 11% YoY.
- Management expects YoY EBITDA margin expansion in H2FY27 but did not reaffirm the 50–70 bps FY27 guidance.
- Morgan Stanley believes margin concerns are already reflected in the valuation.

**Key Takeaway**
- Accelerating India revenue and volume growth support business momentum.
- H2 margin expansion remains a key monitorable.
- Impact: **Positive**

**TATA CONSUMER PRODUCTS – CITI MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Citi maintains **Buy** rating but cuts target price to ₹1,225.
- Consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY, while EBITDA increased 17%.
- India underlying volume growth stood at 11%; salt volumes grew 9%.
- Growth businesses expanded 40%, led by Sampann and ready-to-drink (RTD) products.
- India tea revenue remained soft, while domestic margins faced input cost inflation.
- Pricing actions across multiple categories are yet to fully reflect and may support margin recovery in H2FY27.
- Stronger international and non-branded profitability support consolidated performance.

**Key Takeaway**
- Healthy volume growth and growth businesses continue to drive performance.
- Pricing benefits and international profitability may support margin recovery in H2FY27.
- Impact: **Positive**

**TRIVENI POWER TRANSMISSION – DAM CAPITAL INITIATES BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- DAM Capital initiates coverage with **Buy** rating and a target price of ₹550, implying 20% upside.
- Valuation based on 28x FY29E EV/EBITDA.
- Leading Indian high-speed gearbox manufacturer with global OEM and Navy approvals.
- Offers a 25–30% cost advantage over European peers.
- Order book stands at ₹630 Cr, around 1.8x FY26 revenue, with approximately 60% from defence.
- FY26–FY29E revenue CAGR estimated at 21%.
- EBITDA margin stands at around 35%; EBITDA CAGR projected at 19%.
- RoCE expected to reach around 29% by FY29E.
- Targets over 50% of new-equipment sales from exports.
- GE and Rolls-Royce marine gas-turbine programmes offer additional growth opportunities.

**Key Takeaway**
- Defence-led order visibility, strong margins and export opportunities support growth prospects.
- Execution and delivery of projected growth remain key monitorables.
- Impact: **Positive**

**TATA CONSUMER PRODUCTS – JEFFERIES MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Jefferies maintains **Buy** rating but cuts target price to ₹1,250.

- Growth portfolio share is expected to reach around 50% in the next three years.
- Q2 performance exceeded expectations despite inflationary pressures in tea and salt.
- Product price hikes are expected to support margins ahead.
- International business reported revenue decline but delivered margin expansion.
- FY27 guidance of 50–70 bps YoY EBITDA margin expansion remains unchanged.

**Key Takeaway**
- Growth portfolio expansion and premiumisation support long-term growth.
- Price hikes and margin expansion remain key near-term catalysts.
- Impact: **Positive**

- Operational resilience strengthens confidence in Ather's ability to scale over the long term.

- Market response to the new product remains a key near-term monitorable.

- Stronger bookings and better-than-expected ASPs and margins were key positives.

- Nomura reiterates Ather Energy as its top-two-wheeler pick.

**ONE 97 COMMUNICATIONS (PAYTM) – GOLDMAN SACHS MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Goldman Sachs maintains **Buy** rating with a target price of ₹2,010.
- Q2FY27 revenue grew 28% YoY (33% like-for-like), with further acceleration expected as UPI MDR revenue starts flowing in.
- EBITDA beat Goldman Sachs estimates by 10%, with continued margin expansion.
- UPI MDR could improve payment processing margins by 2.5 bps, potentially contributing ₹800–900 Cr to FY28 EBITDA.
- Financial services growth accelerated, supported by improving personal loan trends.
- Meaningful revenue and EBITDA contribution from postpaid is expected from FY28.
- Payments market share improved for another quarter, with strong monthly transacting user (MTU) additions.
- Higher-than-expected device-related capex may increase depreciation and amortisation costs, leading to some EPS estimate cuts.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong revenue growth, margin expansion and potential UPI MDR benefits support the outlook.
- Higher capex and resulting depreciation costs remain key concerns.
- Impact: **Positive**

**ONE 97 COMMUNICATIONS (PAYTM) – CITI MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Citi maintains **Buy** rating with a target price of ₹1,940.
- Q2 EBITDA and EBIT came 4% and 1% above Citi estimates at ₹270 Cr and ₹120 Cr, respectively.
- Net payment margin increased 0.5 bps QoQ to 9 bps, ahead of Citi's expectations.
- Financial services revenue growth accelerated to 49% YoY from 45% in Q1FY27.
- UPI-MDR is expected to add 2.5 bps to net payment margins, translating to around ₹900 Cr in FY28E.
- Higher DLG share in merchant lending may pressure near-term contribution margins.
- Financial services growth and net payment margins are improving, even excluding UPI-MDR.
- Paytm is increasing investments in AI, marketing, user acquisition and its on-ground sales network.

**Key Takeaway**
- Improving financial services growth and payment margins support the earnings outlook.
- Higher investments and DLG-related costs may weigh on near-term margins.
- Impact: **Positive**

Stock Fundamental in detail

**MANKIND PHARMA – KOTAK MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Kotak maintains **Buy** rating with a target price of ₹3,035.
- Q2FY27 performance was strong, driven by domestic formulations, BSV and international markets.
- Management expects to outperform IPM growth by 1.1–1.2x over the next two quarters.
- Base business recovery is visible through improving volume growth and a richer chronic-care product mix.
- BSV continues to deliver sustained growth momentum.
- OTC business remains the key concern, with growth yet to pick up.
- Kotak expects 23% EPS CAGR over FY26–FY29.

**Key Takeaway**
- Broad-based growth and recovery in the core business support earnings prospects.
- OTC performance remains a key monitorable.
- Impact: **Positive**

Stock Fundamental in detail                            
@Fundamental3

**MANKIND PHARMA – JPMORGAN MAINTAINS NEUTRAL**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- JPMorgan maintains **Neutral** rating with a target price of ₹2,700.
- Q2 revenue came 3% above estimates, driven by strong India Rx and healthy export growth, offsetting consumer business weakness.
- India business grew around 16% YoY, partly supported by a low base.
- EBITDA margin stood at 27%, around 100 bps above estimates.
- FY27 EBITDA margin guidance remains unchanged at 25.5–26.5%.
- Consumer business growth guidance cut to single digits from high-single-digit to double-digit growth.
- Management expects double-digit consumer growth from next year, supported by e-commerce and quick-commerce channels.
- E-commerce and quick-commerce mix rose to around 18% in Q2 from 12% last year.
- EBITDA estimates raised by 3–4% on better visibility in India Rx and exports.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong India Rx, exports and margin performance supported the Q2 beat.
- Sustainable India outperformance and consumer business recovery remain key monitorables.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**MANKIND PHARMA – MACQUARIE MAINTAINS UNDERPERFORM**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Macquarie maintains **Underperform (U-P)** rating with a target price of ₹2,200.
- Q2 revenue, EBITDA and adjusted PAT beat estimates by 3%, 4% and 12%, respectively.
- EBITDA beat was driven by higher revenue, better gross margins, operating leverage and lower R&D expenses.
- PAT beat was supported by higher EBITDA, stronger other income and a slightly lower effective tax rate.
- BSV business remained strong across key brands.
- Consumer healthcare performance remained subdued due to weak category demand and softness in eastern and southern India.
- Net debt declined to ₹2,640 Cr from ₹3,380 Cr in June.
- FY27 EBITDA margin guidance remains at 25.5–26.5%, despite Q2 margin of 27.1%.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong earnings beat and lower net debt support the financial position.
- Weak consumer healthcare performance remains a concern.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**MANKIND PHARMA – BERNSTEIN MAINTAINS UNDERWEIGHT**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Bernstein maintains **Underweight (UW)** rating with a target price of ₹2,057.
- Q2FY27 results offered limited evidence to justify the company's premium valuation.
- Domestic business grew 15.9%, with gastro and vitamins improving, while anti-infectives grew 5.4% and consumer healthcare just 1.2%.
- Volume growth stood at 6.7%, supported by seasonal acute demand and an easier GST-affected base.
- New brand contribution remained limited, raising concerns about the sustainability of headline growth.
- Consumer recovery has been delayed again, highlighting concerns around weakening momentum and slow brand creation.
- Exports performed better than expected, while BSV continued to show improved execution.
- Margins beat estimates, but management retained its 25% margin guidance.

**Key Takeaway**
- Domestic growth and exports offer support, but recovery remains uneven.
- Consumer weakness, limited new-brand traction and premium valuation remain key concerns.
- Impact: **Negative**

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
